html:
Chad is a large, landlocked country in north central Africa, reaching from the Sahara to the savanna, with its capital at N'Djamena. On the map it covers French rule and the republic of 1960.

The Sahel strip around Lake Chad was home to states that lived on trade across the Sahara: Kanem-Bornu, Bagirmi and Wadai. France won the area at the Battle of Kousséri in 1900, where the warlord Rabih az-Zubayr was killed, and made it part of French Equatorial Africa.

  • 1940: governor Félix Éboué took Chad over to Free France, the first colony to do so.
  • 1960: independence.
  • 1965: a long civil war began, between the government of the Christian south and northern rebels.
  • 1982 to 1990: Hissène Habré, later convicted of crimes against humanity; he drove Libyan troops out in 1987.
  • 1990 to 2021: Idriss Déby, followed by his son.

Lake Chad has shrunk sharply since the 1960s, hit by the Sahel drought and irrigation.
sum: Chad is a large, landlocked country in north central Africa, reaching from the Sahara to the savanna, with its capital at N'Djamena. On the map it covers French rule and the republic of 1960.
